title: Planning a Trip
summary: Two friends discuss a two-week trip to Japan: itinerary, budget, and what to pack.
description: An intermediate-level planning conversation. Learners hear modals of suggestion ('we could…', 'let's…'), money expressions, and travel vocabulary (itinerary, budget, accommodation).

vocabulary.definition: a detailed plan of a journey, including places and times
the amount of money you can spend on something
a place to stay, like a hotel or hostel
to arrange something before you need it
visiting interesting places as a tourist

dialogue.text: So, Emma, are you ready to plan our trip to Japan?
Almost. We have two weeks and a budget of two thousand euros each.
Perfect. I think we should book accommodation in advance. Hotels fill up quickly.
Good idea. Maybe we can stay in small guesthouses to save money.
I agree. What about the itinerary? I would love to visit Kyoto.
Kyoto is a must. We could spend four days there, doing some sightseeing.
And we should keep a couple of free days for spontaneous plans.
Exactly. We could also take a day trip to Nara if we have time.
Light clothes, comfortable shoes, and a small backpack for day trips.

questions.q: How much is the budget per person?
Which city is a 'must' according to Emma?

trueFalse.statement: They plan to book hotels at the last minute.
trueFalse.explanation: The speaker says 'we should book accommodation in advance.'

trueFalse.statement: Emma suggests staying in small guesthouses.
trueFalse.explanation: Emma says 'Maybe we can stay in small guesthouses to save money.'

teacherTips: Pre-teach 'we could…' and 'let's…' as planning phrases. Recycle modal verbs of suggestion.
After listening, students plan a short trip in pairs using the same structure (where, how long, budget, must-see places).
Extension: present the plan to the class in a one-minute talk.

es.title: Planificar un viaje
es.summary: Dos amigos hablan de un viaje de dos semanas a Japón: itinerario, presupuesto y qué meter en la maleta.
es.description: Una conversación intermedia de planificación. Los estudiantes oyen modales de sugerencia ('we could…', 'let's…'), expresiones de dinero y vocabulario de viaje (itinerary, budget, accommodation).

vocabulary.definition: un plan detallado de un viaje, con lugares y horarios
la cantidad de dinero que puedes gastar en algo
un lugar donde alojarse, como un hotel o un albergue
reservar algo antes de que lo necesites
visitar lugares de interés como turista

questions.q: ¿Qué ciudad es, según Emma, una visita obligada?

trueFalse.statement: Planean reservar hoteles a última hora.
trueFalse.explanation: El interlocutor dice 'we should book accommodation in advance'.

trueFalse.statement: Emma sugiere alojarse en pequeños hostales.
trueFalse.explanation: Emma dice 'Maybe we can stay in small guesthouses to save money'.

teacherTips: Enseña antes 'we could…' y 'let's…' como frases para planificar. Recicla los verbos modales de sugerencia.
Después de escuchar, los estudiantes planifican un viaje corto por parejas usando la misma estructura (dónde, cuánto tiempo, presupuesto, lugares imprescindibles).
Ampliación: presentan el plan a la clase en una exposición de un minuto.
